summary: Structurally the same pattern — filled/wireframe polygons floating and spinning over a black 16x16 grid, with matching Type/Size/Floaters/Filled/Spin/Line semantics — but the port replaces the original's fixed 5-colour 80s palette with a ~17-hue rainbow, animates 2-3x too slowly at every matched Speed setting, and renders almost nothing at untouched defaults where the original is a bright filled scene.
observations: Rig is grid 16x16, 256 px. Both sides compile and run with no errors at every setting tried; neither freezes, decays or saturates. Untouched 180 s survey and 60 s dialed survey show no mode rotation or regime boundaries on either side — one continuous regime throughout, so there was no separate regime to park in; late windows were checked instead (--skip 40, and a 30 s seed-7 run).

PALETTE (the biggest colour finding). Union of 13 --dump frames spread over a 100 s dialed window on the default rig: the original emits EXACTLY 5 non-black colours, ever — (255,0,99) hot pink, (0,201,255) sky cyan, (0,255,2) green, (104,0,255) violet, (255,206,0) golden yellow — plus pure black. The port over the same window emits 17 non-black colours spread evenly round the hue wheel, including hues the original never produces: (255,83,0) orange, (255,6,0) red, (0,255,185) teal, (197,255,0) chartreuse, (0,95,255) blue, (255,0,222) magenta. So the port is a continuous/finely-quantised rainbow where the original is a fixed 5-entry palette; on screen the original reads as hot-pink/cyan/green/yellow/violet and the port as a general-purpose rainbow.

MOTION SPEED. At identical dials (all controls 0.5) the original's mean frame-to-frame motion is 23 and the port's is 10; over a 60 s dialed survey 42 vs 33; on the --skip 40 late window 33 vs 11. The 12-frame motion filmstrips at 20 fps make it visible: across 0.55 s the original's scene fully reconfigures (its pink triangle grows and rotates through several shapes' worth of travel) while the port's purple triangle drifts a couple of pixels. The port is roughly 2-3x too slow.

SPEED DIAL RANGE. Original Speed 0 -> 1 moves mean motion from 12 to 35 (~3x span, and at Speed=1 the filmstrip shows shapes sweeping across the grid frame by frame). Port Speed 0 -> 1 moves motion only 8 -> 11 (~1.4x span, still a slow drift at maximum). The port's Speed dial is both far weaker and topped out well below the original's mid setting.

UNTOUCHED DEFAULTS diverge badly. Original untouched: mean brightness 117, crisp flat fills of the 5-colour palette, 13% black pixels. Port untouched: mean brightness 26, 62% pure-black pixels, and the rest are ~270 distinct dim blended values (e.g. 120,7,17 / 38,145,39 / 212,157,162) plus a scattering of pure white (255,255,255) specks. Visually the original opens as a bright filled scene of big triangles and the port as a nearly-black tangle of faint broken outlines with white sparkles.

LINE RENDERING. With Filled off and Line at 0 on both sides, the original still draws CONTINUOUS 1-px wireframe outlines in full-saturation palette colours (mean 71); the port draws BROKEN, dotted, disconnected fragments (mean 31) - its thinnest stroke does not produce a continuous line. This is very likely what makes the untouched default look empty.

FLAT POLARITY IS INVERTED. Original Flat high (0.75/1.0) gives mean 89 / motion 28 and a look of more, smaller, well-separated shapes with lots of black; Original Flat low gives mean 114 / motion 23, fewer larger overlapping shapes. The port is the other way round: Flat 0 gives mean 115 / motion 29 and the more/smaller/separated look, Flat >=0.25 gives mean 131 / motion 10 and the fewer/larger look. orig Flat=1 corresponds to port Flat=0.

CONTROL SURFACE MISMATCH. Original: sliderFloaters, sliderType, sliderSize, sliderSpeed, sliderFilled, sliderLine, sliderCutoff, sliderSpin, sliderFlat — nine sliders. Port: sliderNumberOfFloaters, sliderShapeType, sliderSize, sliderSpeed, toggleFilled, sliderLineWidth, sliderCutoff, toggleSpin, toggleFlat. Three names differ (Floaters/NumberOfFloaters, Type/ShapeType, Line/LineWidth) and three kinds differ (Filled, Spin, Flat are sliders on the original and toggles on the port).

Functionally the three renamed-to-toggle dials behave as booleans on BOTH sides, so the kind change is cosmetic in effect — but the switch THRESHOLDS differ. Sweeping 0/0.25/0.5/0.75/1: the original's Filled and Spin flip between 0.25 and 0.5 and its Flat flips between 0.5 and 0.75; every port toggle flips between 0 and 0.25. Any nonzero value turns a port toggle on.

DEGENERATE ENDS. Floaters=0 renders the original completely black (mean 0, motion 0); the port still draws two large shapes (mean 48). Size=0 likewise blacks the original out (mean 0); the port draws ~15 small blobs (mean 37). The port's Floaters and Size dials have a nonzero floor the original does not.

Structure at matched dials is otherwise a good match. Type=0: both draw large soft circles. Type=0.5: both draw hard-edged triangles. Type=1: both collapse to one screen-filling blob. Floaters=1: both fill the frame with overlapping shapes and almost no black. Filled off: both switch to wireframe outlines of the same shapes. Shape counts and sizes track together across the Size and Floaters sweeps on the default rig.

Character holds on a second seed (seed 7, 30 s, Filled/Spin on, Flat matched for the inverted polarity): both sides show overlapping saturated polygons over black with similar shape counts; motion 27 vs 20. The remaining visible differences are the same two — the port's wider hue set and its slower drift.

dials.name: Floaters / NumberOfFloaters
dials.origEffect: Shape count. 0 = completely black (no floaters at all); 0.5 = a few large shapes with black gaps; 1 = frame packed with overlapping shapes, almost no black (mean 128).
dials.portEffect: Same direction and roughly the same top end (mean 128 at 1, frame packed), but 0 does NOT empty the scene — two large shapes still drawn (mean 48).

dials.name: Type / ShapeType
dials.origEffect: Shape kind. 0 = large soft circles; 0.5 = hard-edged triangles; 1 = one screen-filling blob with straight edges.
dials.portEffect: Same progression: 0 = circles, 0.5 = triangles, 1 = one screen-filling blob (rounder than the original's at 1).

dials.name: Size
dials.origEffect: Shape size. 0 = nothing drawn at all (black); 1 = a couple of huge shapes covering the grid.
dials.portEffect: 1 matches (huge shapes, mean 132), but 0 leaves ~15 small blobs rather than an empty frame.

dials.name: Speed
dials.origEffect: Drift/rotation rate. Motion 12 at 0, 35 at 1; at 1 shapes visibly sweep across the grid frame to frame.
dials.portEffect: Same direction but far weaker and far slower: motion 8 at 0, 11 at 1; even at 1 shapes only creep a pixel or two per frame.

dials.name: Filled / toggleFilled
dials.origEffect: Boolean-like: low = wireframe outlines of the shapes (mean 94, motion 53), high = solid fills (mean 114, motion 23). Flips between 0.25 and 0.5.
dials.portEffect: Same two states in the same polarity (low = outlines mean 111, high = fills mean 131), but flips between 0 and 0.25.

dials.name: Line / LineWidth
dials.origEffect: Outline thickness (only meaningful with Filled off). 0 = continuous 1-px wireframes in full-saturation colours (mean 71); 1 = thick strokes (mean 107).
dials.portEffect: Same direction with a much wider range (mean 31 -> 129), but at 0 the strokes break up into disconnected dots and fragments instead of staying continuous.

dials.name: Cutoff
dials.origEffect: No visible effect. Probe delta 0.69; a manual 0-vs-1 sweep over a 60 s window (many shape events) gives mean 100/motion 39 vs 102/42 — dial effect unverifiable from output.
dials.portEffect: Also effectively inert over the same 60 s window: 121/29 vs 122/33.

dials.name: Spin / toggleSpin
dials.origEffect: Boolean-like rotation on/off: motion 20 off vs 23 on; shapes rotate as well as translate when on. Flips between 0.25 and 0.5.
dials.portEffect: Same polarity and same small motion delta (7 off vs 10 on); flips between 0 and 0.25.

dials.name: Flat / toggleFlat
dials.origEffect: Boolean-like: high (>=0.75) gives more, smaller, well-separated shapes over lots of black (mean 89, motion 28); low gives fewer larger overlapping shapes (mean 114, motion 23).
dials.portEffect: Same two looks but INVERTED: port Flat=0 gives the more/smaller/separated look (mean 115, motion 29) and Flat>=0.25 gives the fewer/larger look (mean 131, motion 10).

feedback: Colour is the headline fix. The original only ever emits five exact RGB values plus black — (255,0,99), (0,201,255), (0,255,2), (104,0,255), (255,206,0) — and picks each shape's colour from that fixed set. The port instead walks a full rainbow and produced 17 distinct hues over the same 100 s window, including orange, red, chartreuse, teal and blue that the original never shows. Constrain the port to that 5-entry palette (verify by dumping frames and counting distinct RGB values: it should be 6 including black, on any window).

Motion is 2-3x too slow at matched Speed. At all-dials-0.5 the original's mean frame-to-frame motion is 23 and the port's is 10; on a late window (t=40-48 s) it is 33 vs 11. Multiply the per-frame drift/rotation step by roughly 2.5-3x.

The Speed dial's range is also too narrow. Original Speed 0->1 spans motion 12->35; the port spans 8->11. Widen the mapping so Speed=1 is a visible sweep across the grid (a shape should traverse several pixels per frame at 20 fps), not a slow creep.

Untouched defaults render near-black on the port (mean brightness 26, 62% black pixels, faint blended outlines plus white specks) where the original renders a bright filled scene (mean 117, flat palette fills, 13% black). Whatever the port's internal defaults are for Filled and LineWidth, set them so the untouched pattern opens as solid filled shapes in full-saturation palette colours like the original does.

The port's thinnest stroke is broken. With Filled off and LineWidth 0, the original draws continuous 1-px wireframe outlines; the port draws disconnected dots and short fragments with gaps along every edge. Raise the minimum stroke width / fix the line rasterisation so the thinnest setting still yields an unbroken outline.
Flat's polarity is reversed. On the original, Flat ON (high) gives many smaller well-separated shapes over lots of black; on the port that look appears at Flat OFF. Invert the port's Flat toggle.

Floaters=0 and Size=0 should empty the frame. The original goes completely black at either extreme (mean 0, motion 0); the port still draws two large shapes at Floaters=0 and ~15 small blobs at Size=0. Remove the nonzero floor on both mappings.

Control surface should mirror the original's: nine SLIDERS named sliderFloaters, sliderType, sliderSize, sliderSpeed, sliderFilled, sliderLine, sliderCutoff, sliderSpin, sliderFlat. The port renames three (NumberOfFloaters, ShapeType, LineWidth) and converts three to toggles (Filled, Spin, Flat). Even though those three behave as booleans on both sides, the original's slider thresholds sit near the middle (Filled and Spin flip between 0.25 and 0.5, Flat between 0.5 and 0.75) whereas every port toggle flips above 0 — restoring sliders with mid-range thresholds fixes both the surface and the threshold mismatch.
Cutoff has no observable effect on either side over a 60 s multi-event window, so no action is needed there; keep the control present since the original exposes it.
